title: 'When you're that sick, you reflect on the values that matter most': Sweden's Birgitta Ohlsson returns to fight the far right
subhead: The former Liberal figure, who had left politics, is now standing with the Center Party in Sweden's general election on Sunday. At 51, after fighting two cancers, the pro-European feminist is determined to take on the extremist drift of her former political camp.

France issues discreet apology to lift US block on new ambassador to Washington
subhead: The French diplomatic service's appointment of Aurélien Lechevallier, who is close to President Emmanuel Macron, had been frozen in the US due to a July 25 statement in which the service criticized Washington's stance on human rights. An official statement of contrition was issued on Friday.

title: 'Ordinary citizens do not want to be sent to a war with no end in sight': Russian men consider exile
subhead: Amid the threat of renewed conscription, some Russian men of fighting age have purchased plane tickets and are ready to leave if a general mobilization is declared after the elections scheduled for September 18 to 20. Georgia, Armenia and Serbia are the most popular destinations.

title: 2027 presidential election: Mélenchon pressures left-wing rivals at Fête de L'Humanité festival
subhead: Jean-Luc Mélenchon, presidential candidate of radical-left La France Insoumise, put on a show of strength and engaged in a long-distance dual with Communist leader Fabien Roussel. Mélenchon also sought to convince crowds that he could beat Marine Le Pen.

title: In southeast France, the deaths of 64 sheep blamed on wolves raise questions
subhead: French wildlife officials say wolves are responsible for a particularly deadly attack in a pasture in the Drôme department in late August. Advocacy groups dispute that assessment, at a time when shootings of wild canid are on the rise.

How 9/11 changed the far right
subhead: The September 11 terrorist attacks marked a turning point for radical right-wing movements. Since then, these political currents have adopted a violently anti-Islam rhetoric, positioning themselves as defenders of a so-called 'Judeo-Christian West.'

title: The forgotten French prisoner of 9/11
subhead: Zacarias Moussaoui, who was sent to the US by Al-Qaeda to prepare attacks and was convicted of complicity in the September 11 attacks, has spent the past 20 years serving a life sentence without the possibility of parole in a high-security penitentiary in Colorado. His lawyer is requesting his transfer to France.

title: French far right gets tangled up in headscarf ban proposal
subhead: Intended as a communications coup, the revival of the long-standing debate within the Rassemblement National over banning the headscarf in public spaces has exposed legal uncertainties and disagreements between Marine Le Pen and Jordan Bardella.
